title: Named-party joinder and representative class actions
shortTitle: Named-party joinder and representative class actions
summary: Joinder combines claims of persons who are individually parties. A class action allows named representatives to litigate for absentees after satisfying the requirements for legitimate representation.
notes: Mussat distinguishes a federal Rule 23 class from the mass action in Bristol-Myers. That distinction does not exempt every absentee from every jurisdictional requirement, as TransUnion demonstrates.

sections.Meaning: Joinder combines claims of persons who are individually parties. A class action allows named representatives to litigate for absentees after satisfying the requirements for legitimate representation.
sections.How to work through the question: Ask whether each claimant is named and participating or belongs to an absent class. Then identify the procedural question: commonality, personal jurisdiction, standing, venue, or preclusion. The status of absentees varies with the issue.
